newsitem.title: USA: Columbus, S.C., buys land for trolley line.
newsitem.headline: Columbus, S.C., buys land for trolley line.

text.p: City officials in Columbus, S.C., have purchased land for a 10-mile trolley line expected to be in full operation by late 1999.
The city announced Monday it had completed the $1.1 million purchase of 10.6 miles of the Warm Springs Rail Corridor and 170 acres of adjoining land from Norfolk Southern Railway Corp.
The first battery-powered trolley, costing about $344,000, is scheduled to begin running by the spring of 1997 between the city's trade center and civic center.

The full 10-mile line is expected to be in operation in time to connect with the city's new performing arts center in late 1999, said city transportation chief Steve Dockter. The completed line will connect the downtown business district with hospitals and medical centers in the Talbotton Road Area, Columbus State University and several malls, parks and public schools.
The land will also be used for hiking and bicycle trails.
